title: Microslice Ledger — Persona-aware Cost Composer & Export Path
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, persona-aware token-level cost composer inside the Redwood Console that lets engineers, finance users, and platform owners build, preview, and export micro-slices of consumption with pricing presets. The Microslice Ledger composes a cost slice by selecting dimensions (route, model variant, user role, session window), applying pricing modifiers (reserved vs. burst, quantization tier), and presenting both a compact on-screen breakdown and CSV export that maps back to billing line items. The goal is to reduce time-to-insight for anomaly triage and to create a repeatable export artefact for chargeback and forecasting.
acceptance_criteria: UI: A compact composer panel that fits in the Console's right rail and scales to full-screen modal for multi-dimension configuration
Attribution: Breakdowns by token origin (system/prompt/assistant), model variant, and route with percent and absolute token counts
Pricing presets: Three saved presets (dev, prod, reserved) that apply quantization and batch discounts and update cost preview in real time
Export: CSV schema that includes token-level rows, pricing-applied columns, and metadata (route, model-version, timestamp, customer-id) matching billing ledger requirements
Performance: Composer interactions complete within 200ms for dimension toggles and under 1s for applying presets on 30s sample windows
Audit: Every export is recorded in the Console activity log with a downloadable artifact link
design_notes: Compact vs full: We prioritize a condensed right-rail composer to keep context for debugging flows; fallback to an explorable modal for multi-dimension saves
Role-aware defaults: Platform owners need more granular rows while engineers prefer aggregated top-level breakdowns; show segmented defaults per persona
Pricing granularity tradeoff: Showing per-token line items improves auditability but risks performance on large windows — we implement sample windowing and summary rows by default
Export schema: Align fields with billing team's microledger spec (billing_v2) and include mapping keys for downstream ETL
Visual encoding: Use stacked microbars for token origin with hover-to-heatmap for cost hotspots; numeric emphasis on unit cost and aggregated USD

reviews: PM (Arjun Malik): 'Love the persona defaults — please ensure presets are editable and versioned'
Eng (Ellen Park): 'Concern about exporting token-level rows for large sessions; suggest sampling + deterministic hashing to map back to full session'
Billing (Samira Khan): 'CSV schema looks good, include an 'export_checksum' column for reconciliation'
Design Lead (Ibrahim Obeid): 'Consider a compact 'quick-export' action that applies the last-used preset and does a background export with notification'
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decided on sample-windowing default (30s) to avoid massive CSVs; provide 'full-session' override gated behind an explicit warning
Chosen export schema aligns with billing_v2 to minimize ETL work even if it increases column count in CSV
Opted for role-aware defaults over global toggles to surface relevant controls to each persona without hiding advanced options
risks_and_mitigation: Large exports could hit memory quotas: Mitigation — asynchronous export pipeline with chunked writes and notification link
Confusing pricing language for non-finance users: Mitigation — inline tooltips, sample-calculation view, and A/B copy tests
Mismatch between previewed cost and final invoice due to rounding/discount windows: Mitigation — include 'estimated' badge and link to billing documentation
next_steps: Finalize copy for pricing presets and run two A/B microcopy tests (target cohort: existing Dedicated customers)
Hand off specs and export CSV schema to Infra for implementation of asynchronous export job
Deliver accessibility pass on microbar visualizations and test color blindness contrasts
Connect prototype to console feature flag for Canary rollout and collect telemetry on 'export' frequency
notes_for_engineering: API: /costs/microslice/export should accept preset_id, sample_window_seconds, persona, and return an export_job_id
Schema: Ensure CSV contains billing_keys and an 'estimated_usd' column with 4-decimal precision
Telemetry: Emit analytics events for compose_open, preset_apply, export_initiated, export_completed
